title: Section 1557 & AI Translation: September 2026
summary: Learn how Section 1557 applies to AI medical interpretation, written machine translation, qualified interpreters, patient requests.
body_markdown:
###


Section 1557 does not contain a blanket prohibition on live AI medical interpretation. Covered entities still have to provide meaningful access, and they remain responsible for the quality, timeliness, privacy, and patient access of the language assistance they provide.


###


Section 1557 does not create a blanket rule requiring a human interpreter for every spoken encounter. Requirements are context-specific, and organizations should review current HHS guidance, applicable court decisions, patient needs, and their own language-access policy.


###


For written machine translation, the organization must ensure the output meets the applicable accuracy and meaningful-access standard. Validated automated quality controls or a qualified reviewer can provide that review path; a separate human review step is not required for every AI-generated translation.


###


No. HHS defines machine translation as text-based automated translation. Live spoken AI interpretation is a different language-assistance use case, although meaningful-access duties still apply.


###


Opalite can support a healthcare organization’s language-access workflow through real-time AI medical interpretation, Guardian quality monitoring, document translation, and use across in-person, phone, and telehealth settings. The healthcare organization remains responsible for its Section 1557 analysis, policies, and implementation.
